security.title: Security
security.intro: Two-factor authentication for your account: a six-digit code from an authenticator app at every sign-in, backup codes for when the app is unavailable. Every change is recorded in the audit log.

status.title: Two-factor authentication
status.backupCodes: {count, plural, =0 {No backup codes left} one {# backup code left} other {# backup codes left}}
status.textEnabled: Sign-ins need your password and a code from your authenticator app. Generate new backup codes when you run low; disabling removes the second factor and invalidates the codes.
status.textDisabled: Your account is protected by your password alone. Enabling takes a minute: confirm your password, scan a QR code with your authenticator app, enter one code and save your backup codes.

ops.title: Track Operations requires two-factor authentication
ops.textDisabled: Your account holds a platform role. The operations console (/ops) stays closed until two-factor authentication is enabled for your account.
ops.textEnabled: Your account holds a platform role and two-factor authentication is enabled, so the operations console is open to you.

password.label: Password
password.hint: Confirm your password to start the setup.

scan.title: Scan the QR code
scan.text: Open your authenticator app (for example Google Authenticator, 1Password, Microsoft Authenticator or Aegis) and scan the code, or enter the key by hand.
scan.qrAlt: QR code for the authenticator app, account {account}
scan.qrUnavailable: The QR code cannot be shown here; enter the key by hand.
scan.manualText: Time-based code, six digits, every 30 seconds.

verify.title: Enter the code from the app
verify.text: Enter the six-digit code your authenticator app shows right now.
verify.label: Verification code

backup.title: Save your backup codes
backup.text: Each code signs you in once when your authenticator app is unavailable. They are shown only now — copy or download them and keep them somewhere safe.
backup.confirm: I have stored the backup codes somewhere safe.
backup.closeGuard: Tick the box to confirm you stored the codes, then finish. You can generate new codes from this page at any time.

disable.title: Disable two-factor authentication
disable.text: Afterwards your account is protected by your password alone, and your backup codes stop working. Trusted devices are forgotten.
disable.confirm: I understand that my account will be less protected.

regenerate.title: Generate new backup codes
regenerate.text: Ten new codes replace the current ones; the previous codes stop working immediately.

file.title: Track — two-factor backup codes
file.note: Each code works once. Keep this file somewhere safe and delete it when the codes are used.

errors.code: The code is not valid. Check the time on your device and try again.
errors.rateLimited: Too many attempts. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.notEnabled: Two-factor authentication is not enabled for this account.
errors.noPassword: Your account has no password, so this step cannot be confirmed. Set a password first (“Forgot password?” on the sign-in page), then try again.
errors.state: This page is out of date: the two-factor status has changed in the meantime. Reload the page.
errors.session: Your session has ended. Sign in again and try once more.
errors.audit: The change was applied but could not be recorded in the audit log. Reload the page; if this keeps happening, contact support.
errors.generic: That did not work. Please try again.
